name: F_{net} = ma
e: Newton's second law is F_net = ma. Circular motion still needs a net inward force because centripetal acceleration is not zero.

name: F_c = m a_c = \frac{m v^2}{r}
e: The centripetal force magnitude is F_c = m a_c = mv²/r. Faster motion or a tighter radius needs a larger inward force.

name: F_c = m r \omega^2
content: Magnitude of the centripetal force in terms of angular velocity
e: In terms of angular speed, F_c = m r ω². This is mv²/r after v = rω is substituted, so F_c grows with ω².

name: F_f = \frac{m v^2}{r}
content: Force for a car of mass m and speed v on a path of radius r
e: On a level curve the friction that keeps a car of mass m and speed v on radius r is F_f = mv²/r. That friction is the centripetal force.

name: \tan \theta = \frac{v^2}{rg}
content: Banking angle of a road chosen for the limiting speed v
e: The banking angle chosen for limiting speed v satisfies tanθ = v²/(rg). A larger v or a smaller r needs a steeper bank.
